expert.question: In Romans 8:26-27, how does the Holy Spirit assist the prayer of the believer in his weakness?
options: By himself interceding for the saints according to God with 'inexpressible groans' when we do not know what to ask
expert.explanation: The believer thus benefits from a double divine intercession: the Spirit in him (v. 26) and Christ at the right hand of God (v. 34).

expert.question: What is the meaning of the expression 'to have one's loins girded' (Luke 12:35; Ephesians 6:14; 1 Peter 1:13)?
options: Raise and tie the long tails of your tunic with a belt to be ready to act, run or leave without hindrance — a symbol of spiritual vigilance
expert.explanation: Recalling the night of Passover in Exodus 12:11, this image calls believers to lucidity and immediate availability.

expert.question: In 1 Corinthians 15:44 ('the animal/psychic body is sown, the spiritual body is raised'), what does 'spiritual body' (sôma pneumatikon) mean?
options: An immaterial ghost without a body
A true, physical, glorious body, fully animated, renewed and quickened by the Holy Spirit (like the resurrected body of Christ)
A soul freed from all matter
expert.explanation: The adjective 'pneumatikon' does not oppose 'immaterial' to 'material', but 'animated by the imperishable Spirit' to 'subject to mortal weakness' (v. 42-44).

expert.question: In James 1:25, why does the author call the gospel 'the perfect law, the law of liberty'?
options: Because it allows you to do anything
Because accomplished by the Spirit and love (royal law of James 2:8), it frees the believer to obey voluntarily from within rather than by servile compulsion
expert.explanation: He who applies himself to it with perseverance and puts it into practice is blessed in his very action.

expert.question: In 1 Peter 2:2 ('desire as newborn children the spiritual and pure milk'), what Greek adjective ('logikon') is translated as 'spiritual'?
options: Logikon ('rational/according to the Word/spiritual', close to Romans 12:1)
expert.explanation: Just after celebrating the 'living and permanent word of God' (1:23-25), Peter calls us to feed greedily on this pure Word in order to grow towards salvation.

expert.question: In 2 Corinthians 4:7 ('We bear this treasure in earthen vessels'), what ministerial truth does Paul state?
options: That the apostles must be rich
The human frailty of the messengers highlights that sovereign power comes from God and not from us
That the human body is bad
That the Gospel must remain hidden
expert.explanation: The weakness and trials of the servant become the scene in which the life of Jesus is manifested (2 Corinthians 4:8-11).

expert.question: In Matthew 5:17-20, what does 'except your righteousness surpass that of the scribes and Pharisees' mean?
options: An inner righteousness of the heart, rooted in grace and faithful love that fulfills the deeper intent of the Law rather than its legalistic appearance
expert.explanation: The following six antitheses ("You have heard... but I tell you", ch. 5) illustrate this justice of the heart extending to the love of enemies.

expert.question: In John 14:2 ('There are many mansions in my Father's house'), what is the meaning of the Greek word 'monai'?
options: Permanent dwellings/places of lasting residence with the Father in eternal communion
expert.explanation: This term is from the same root as the verb 'menein' (dwell) used in John 14:23 ('we will make our abode with him').

expert.question: In Romans 11:36 ('Of him, through him, and for him are all things'), what threefold relationship of God to the universe is proclaimed?
options: God is the original Source ('from him'), the Sustaining Means ('through him') and the Final Goal ('for him') of all reality
expert.explanation: This doxology concludes the eleven doctrinal chapters of Romans before the practical exhortation of Romans 12.

expert.question: In Psalm 139:7-10 ('Where shall I go from your Spirit?'), what divine attribute does the psalmist ponder in wonder rather than fear?
options: The personal and benevolent omnipresence of God who sustains the believer even in the remotest extremities
expert.explanation: Far from fleeing a hostile spy, David discovers that even at the ends of the seas 'your right hand will seize me'.

expert.question: In Isaiah 40:28-31, on what basis does the prophet rest the hope of the weary (“He gives strength to the weary”)?
options: On the strength of the army of Judah
On the inexhaustible transcendence of the Creator God who never tires nor tires and whose intelligence is unfathomable
expert.explanation: Waiting/hoping in the Lord (qawah) allows you to receive wings like eagles and to walk without getting tired.

expert.question: In 1 Timothy 3:16, what is the literary genre and content of the passage 'He who was manifested in the flesh, justified by the Spirit...'?
options: An early Christological hymn of six parallel lines summarizing the incarnation, the vindication by the Spirit, the angelic testimony, the preaching to the nations, the faith of the world and the ascension into glory
expert.explanation: This hymn is described by Paul as 'the great mystery of godliness'.

expert.question: In Hebrews 12:22-24, what spiritual reality have New Covenant believers already approached?
options: Mount Zion, the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, myriads of angels and Jesus mediator of the new covenant
expert.explanation: The confident access to the presence of God in Christ contrasts with the sacred terror that surrounded Sinai.

expert.question: In 1 Corinthians 2:9 ('Eye has not seen these things...'), how does Paul respond to v. 10 on access to these realities?
options: No one will ever know them for a thousand years
'God has revealed them to us through the Spirit. For the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God'
We find them by logic alone
expert.explanation: Often wrongly cited as speaking only of the future heaven, this text first describes the hidden wisdom of the cross revealed now by the Spirit.

expert.question: In Titus 3:5 ('he has saved us, not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy, by the washing of regeneration and renewing of the Holy Spirit'), what does 'paliggenesia' (regeneration) mean?
options: A 'new birth/new genesis' carried out by the Holy Spirit who radically renews the heart
A purely symbolic rite without faith
expert.explanation: The term does not appear elsewhere in the NT until Matthew 19:28 for the final cosmic renewal.

expert.question: In Psalm 119:11 ('Thy word I hold fast in my heart, that I may not sin against thee'), what spiritual connection is made?
options: Loving interiorization and memorization of the Word of God as a moral defense against temptation
expert.explanation: Hiding (tsaphan) the Word like a treasure in the heart transforms our desires and protects our steps.

expert.question: In Matthew 5:13 ('You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt loses its flavor...'), what function of the disciple in the world is emphasized?
options: Withdraw from the world into the desert
Preserve from moral corruption and give taste/witness through distinct loyalty within society
expert.explanation: Just like light (v. 14), salt does not exist for its own sake but to act at the heart of the world without losing its identity.

expert.question: In 2 Corinthians 1:20 ('As for all the promises of God, in him is yes'), what hermeneutical key does Paul give?
options: That every promise of the OT is canceled
May all divine promises find their confirmation and definitive fulfillment in Jesus Christ, hence our 'Amen' to the glory of God
That the OT does not speak of Jesus
expert.explanation: Christ is the faithful guarantor of the word of God, in opposition to human inconstancy.

expert.question: In John 7:37-39 ("If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink... rivers of living water will flow from his bosom"), what does John say Jesus was referring to?
options: To the Holy Spirit that those who believed in him were to receive after his glorification
expert.explanation: Jesus spoke these words on the last day of the Feast of Tabernacles, marked by the libations of water at the Temple.

expert.question: In Galatians 6:2 ('Bear one another's burdens, and thus you will fulfill the law of Christ'), what is 'the law of Christ'?
options: The law of practical brotherly love and humble service following the example of Jesus (John 13:34; Galatians 5:14)
expert.explanation: In Galatians 6:5, Paul then specifies that each person will bear his own burden of responsibility before God — the complementarity of mutual help and responsibility.

expert.question: In 1 Peter 4:10, how should each believer use the spiritual gift (charisma) he has received?
options: As good dispensers (stewards) of the various graces of God, serving one another
expert.explanation: The gift is a grace entrusted in stewardship to build up the Church so that God may be glorified in all things through Jesus Christ (v. 11).

expert.question: In Romans 14:17 ('For the kingdom of God is not eating and drinking, but...'), what three fruits characterize the Kingdom?
options: Righteousness, peace and joy, through the Holy Spirit
expert.explanation: Paul relativizes the quarrels over days and foods to refocus the Church on the essentials of the Kingdom.

expert.question: In Psalm 34:8 (34:9: 'Smell and see how good the LORD is!'), what Hebrew verb is used for 'smell/taste'?
options: Tasting (ta'am) — invitation to a personal and confident experience of God's goodness, echoed in 1 Peter 2:3
expert.explanation: 'Blessed is the man who seeks refuge in himself!' concludes this verse.

expert.question: In Matthew 25:40 ('Inasmuch as you did these things to one of the least of these my brethren, you did them to me'), what Christological truth is taught?
options: May Jesus personally identify with his people in need (starving, foreigners, sick, prisoners) and judge the authenticity of faith through concrete charity
That only the rich are judged
expert.explanation: Service to the most vulnerable demonstrates real love for the King himself.

expert.question: In 2 Peter 1:3-4, what has already been given to the believer through the knowledge of him who called us?
options: All that contributes to life and godliness, as well as the greater and more precious promises in order to participate in the divine nature
expert.explanation: To participate in the 'divine nature' means to reflect the moral holiness and love of God by fleeing the corruption of the world.

expert.question: In Ephesians 3:20-21, how does Paul express the measure of God's power at work in the Church?
options: 'He who can do, through the power that works within us, infinitely beyond all that we ask or think'
expert.explanation: This doxology concludes Paul's prayer for believers to grasp the breadth, length, depth, and height of Christ's love.

expert.question: In John 1:16 ('And of his fullness have we all received, and grace for grace'), what does 'grace for grace' (charin anti charitos) mean?
options: A grace that quickly runs out
An uninterrupted and superabundant succession of graces (a new grace constantly replacing or adding to the previous one, or the grace of the Gospel succeeding that of the Law)
A grace reserved for John alone
expert.explanation: This verse expresses the inexhaustible generosity of Christ, compared to v. 17 to the Law given by Moses.

expert.question: In Psalm 130:3-4 ('If you keep in remembrance of iniquities, O LORD, who can stand? But...'), on what is the true fear of God based?
options: 'But forgiveness is with you, that you may be feared' — free forgiveness inspires loving and grateful respect
expert.explanation: Far from encouraging levity, the discovery of divine forgiveness engenders a deep reverence towards God.

expert.question: In Acts 17:28 ('In him we have life, and movement, and being'), how does Paul use Greek culture in Athens?
options: By quoting Greek poets (Epimenides / Aratos: 'We are of his race') to show that man depends on the Creator God and must reject idols
expert.explanation: Paul builds an intelligent cultural bridge without ever compromising the final call to repentance and resurrection (vv. 30-31).

expert.question: In Philippians 4:11-13, what is the exact context of the famous verse 'I can do all things through him who strengthens me'?
options: The promise of succeeding in any sporting or financial endeavor effortlessly
The secret of contentment learned by Paul: knowing how to live in humiliation/dearth as well as in abundance thanks to the inner strength of Christ
expert.explanation: Placed in context, this verse teaches spiritual independence and inner peace in all circumstances.

expert.question: In Jeremiah 17:9-10 ('The heart is devious above all things, and is wicked: who can know it?'), what response does v. 10 does it bring?
options: 'I, the LORD, test the heart, I search the reins, to reward each man according to his ways'
expert.explanation: This lucid diagnosis of the human condition explains the need for a new heart promised in Jeremiah 31 and Ezekiel 36.

expert.question: In Hebrews 10:19-22, what three privileges flow from our 'free entry into the sanctuary by the blood of Jesus'?
options: Let us draw near with a sincere heart in the fullness of faith, hold fast to the profession of our hope, and watch over one another to stir one another up to love.
expert.explanation: The three theological virtues (faith, hope, love) flow directly from the access opened by the sacrifice of Christ.

expert.question: In 1 Thessalonians 5:16-18 ('Be joyful always. Pray without ceasing. In all things give thanks'), what important clarification accompanies 'in all things'?
options: 'For this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you' — giving thanks IN THE MIDDLE of every circumstance (not necessarily FOR the evil itself)
Let the prayer last 24 hours without speaking
expert.explanation: Gratitude rests on the sovereign faithfulness of God in Christ within each situation.

expert.question: In 1 John 2:15-17, how does John describe the three lusts that sum up 'all that is in the world'?
options: The lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life—these pass away, but he who does the will of God abides forever
Youth, middle age and old age
expert.explanation: This triptych recalls both the temptation of Eve in Genesis 3:6 and the temptations of Jesus in the desert.

expert.question: In Luke 9:23-24, what paradox does Jesus state about the true meaning of life?
options: 'Whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses it for my sake will save it'
expert.explanation: This paradox is repeated in the four Gospels (Matthew 10:39; 16:25; Mark 8:35; John 12:25) as it is central to the teaching of Jesus.

expert.question: In Amos 5:24, what famous image of social and spiritual justice does the prophet proclaim?
options: 'But let righteousness flow like a stream of water, and righteousness like a torrent that never runs dry!'
expert.explanation: Amos contrasts loud songs without justice with an endless river of equity and righteousness.

expert.question: In Psalm 110:3, how do the people of the Messiah-King present themselves in the day of his power?
options: Full of good will (voluntary offerings), clothed in sacred ornaments, like the rising dew of dawn
expert.explanation: Poetic image of a young army, pure and voluntarily devoted to its King.

expert.question: In Romans 15:4, what pastoral role does Paul assign to all Old Testament Scriptures?
options: 'Whatever was written in advance was written for our instruction, so that through patience and the comfort of the Scriptures we might have hope.'
expert.explanation: Paul affirms the ongoing spiritual and comforting relevance of the Old Testament for the Church.

expert.question: In 2 Timothy 2:15, what ideal does Paul propose for God's servant in the face of Scripture?
options: 'Strive to present yourself before God as a proven man, a worker who does not need to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.'
expert.explanation: 'To dispense rightly' (orthotomeô) literally means 'to trace a furrow straight / to cut out accurately' the Word without twisting it.

expert.question: In Revelation 1:5-6, how does the opening doxology summarize the past and present work of Christ?
options: He will judge us without mercy
'To him who loves us, who has delivered us from our sins by his blood, and has made us a kingdom, priests to God his Father'
expert.explanation: The present tense 'who loves us' underlines the present and continuing love of the resurrected Christ founded on his cross.
